marie: Heads up — we saw a 3x tail-latency spike on llama3-13b hosted inference ~2026-03-18T15:05Z. Quick triage: runtime picked the fallback_gemm kernel for ~12% of chat requests using the new prefix padding flow. Suspect RoPE theta scaling + KV-slice alignment off-by-1 interaction. Repro and notes below.

marie: repro (local):
```bash
# minimal repro: send chat request with odd prefix length + short response window
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/infer \\n  -d '{"model":"llama3-13b","input":"<system>...<user>hi</user>","chat_prefix_len":37}'
```
I attached a short perf trace — you can see kernel_selector logged reason=STRIDE_MISMATCH and then fallback_gemm used.

perf-bot: quick profile summary: fallback_gemm accounts for +220ms p99 regression on those requests.
```
# kernel selector snippet
selector: model=llama3-13b ver=3.2
reason=kv_stride_mismatch (prefix_len % 8 != 0) -> chosen=fallback_gemm
fast_gemm: expected stride=8, actual=5
```

devin: interesting — prefix pad producing non-8-aligned KV slices. Are we aligning based on head_dim or hidden_size?

marie: current code aligns to head_dim*bytes_per_elem and then to 8 bytes for vectorization. Llama3 variant uses head_dim=128 so usually aligned, but chat prefix variability created odd effective stride when we chop prefixes per-turn.

kai: quick mitigation: allow selector to prefer fast_gemm when sequence_len <= 64 even if stride != 8. That will cover chat UX cases. Patch sketch:
```diff
- if (stride_mismatch) return fallback_gemm;
+ if (stride_mismatch && seq_len > 64) return fallback_gemm;
+ // short chats: prefer fast path to avoid tail latency spikes
```
Can we canary that? @devin?

devin: +1 to canary. I'll flip RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=prefer_fast_small_seq on a single dedicated shard for model=llama3-13b ver=3.2 and run synthetic load with prefix_len odd values.

sophia: also want to add a guard in the tokenizer path: normalize prefix padding to even multiples of 8 when safe. That reduces selector surprises and keeps semantics identical for most prompts. But watch tokens that are semantically significant — only pad system/joiner tokens.

marie: good call. Plan: 1) canary selector tweak (devin), 2) tokenizer normalize pad (sophia), 3) follow-up: add unit test for kv_stride edgecases and a perf regression alert for fallback_gemm jumps.

kai: I'll draft the canary config and rollout notes. ping me when you have the synthetic results. :eyes:

devin: started canary job @ 3332101280, running 10k chat requests with varying prefix_len. preliminary: p99 dropped from +220ms extra to +30ms for canary. pushing logs to /opt/perf/canary/3332101280.log

marie: awesome — once canary stable let's ship tokenizer pad normalize and a small kernel-selector unit test. Thanks all :thumbsup:
